# Introducing Classmates: A New Way for U.S. College Students to Connect on Roblox


New Feature Helps Students Find Other Roblox Players


By


Roblox Staff


Published


Nov 18, 2026


As colleges across the U.S. launch on-campus[Roblox clubs](https://www.instagram.com/unt_roblox_club) , students are sharing their stories on Instagram and looking for more players. Students[say these clubs](https://baylorlariat.com/2026/10/05/roblox-club-enters-digital-arena/) , which have taken off in the past couple of months, are where they can make friends, have fun, and take a study break. That’s why we’re introducing[Classmates](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/52432178088084-Classmates-on-Roblox) , a new feature that makes it easier for U.S. college students to find other Roblox players at their school. Starting today, it’s available to students at any U.S. college or university, and we may expand to more schools or regions in the future.


With Roblox clubs popping up at over 100 colleges across 30 states, Classmates gives students a new way to grow these communities and play together. To get started, students opt in with their school-provided email and then look for other students at their college or university. School names are used only to help players find each other, and only classmates from the same school will see one another’s affiliation.


The Classmates feature will appear where players go to add Friends. They’ll be prompted to enter their school email address to see other verified students from their college or university.


“People play it \[Roblox\] all the time in college. Our first mass meeting had 60-plus people attend, and[that post](https://www.instagram.com/p/Ddca5phCaXK/?obrf=a2EzcXlxcjB1NXh0) had a million views alone,” said Alexander Villagomez, founder and president of the Roblox Club at the University of Michigan. “Thousands and thousands of people have reposted our posts and sent them to their friends. People really engage with seeing students having fun with Roblox.”


“I didn’t see as many clubs on campus where people could really just come and have a fun time,” said Rabab Zehra, who started the[Roblox Club](https://www.instagram.com/p/DeQAsysGsz_/?img_index=1) at the University of North Texas. “In college, a lot of people are kind of isolated, especially if you’re a commuter, so you don’t really have as many opportunities to make new friends.”


“Everyone’s just so nervous about seeming cool to one another,” said Tayler Donaldson, co-president of the[Roblox Club](https://www.tiktok.com/@sdsuroblox/photo/7692104479935679774) at San Diego State University. “And this is just a place where it’s like, we’re more similar than we think we are.”


Players 18 and older are the[fastest-growing cohort on Roblox](https://s27.q4cdn.com/984876518/files/content_files/Q3-2026-Earnings-Shareholder-Letter.pdf) . As of October 31, 2026, users 18 and older represented 29% of global age-checked daily active users, continuing the recent steady growth of that age group. With these clubs, players who’ve grown up with Roblox are bringing it into their next chapter, making it part of their college experience.


We’re excited to help them build these communities with Classmates!
